Subject: Embeddings integration: vector dimensions, batching, normalization - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to connect and learn more about Acme's search & recommendations roadmap. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Call highlights:
- You currently use VendorX for embeddings (512-d), with an offline vector store and live re-ranking on top of BM25 + cosine.
- Average document length ~1.5k tokens; queries are short (3-10 tokens).
- Important constraints: per-request latency <= 150ms for queries, secure VPC-only traffic to your vector DB, and strict PII handling.

Integration notes / qualification questions (for engineering):
- Vector dims: You mentioned VendorX uses 512-d. Are you open to switching to 768 or 1024 if it improves recall?
- Normalization: Do you store normalized vectors (L2) currently, or rely on raw vectors + runtime normalization?
- Batching: What is your typical query QPS? Any burst patterns (e.g., 500 QPS for flash events)?
- Migration: How big is your index? You said "couple million docs" — can you confirm approximate vector count and size (GB)?

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical sync with your engineering team (30-45m) — Dev, Rishi & I can join.
2) We'll provide a small sample integration guide and a sample export CSV you can run through our SDK.
3) If the sample looks good, we schedule a migration plan for zero-downtime reindex + A/B test.

I've attached a small sample export you mentioned (embeddings_export_sample.csv) and a short integration guide.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few answers to the engineering questions you raised:

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: vector dimensions, batching, normalization - technical notes

Alex — thanks for the details, this helps a lot. Quick technical notes so the sync can be focused: 

- Normalization: We support either normalized vectors at write time (recommended) or runtime normalization during nearest-neighbor scoring. Since you already store L2-normalized vectors, that aligns well and avoids extra compute at query time.

- Vector dims: Our curated model zoo includes 512, 768, and 1024 variants. Given your 512 baseline and index size (2.2M), moving to 768 could improve recall but will increase storage and cost (~1.5x storage). For an A/B test we usually suggest keeping the existing 512 capture window and running a parallel reindex of a sample shard at 768 to measure lift.

- Batching & throughput: For your spike behavior (650 QPS), we'll recommend the following in the deployment config:
  * Request-level batching enabled with max_batch_size=128 and target_batch_latency_ms=20.
  * KV/prefix caching for the common short queries to reduce decoder work.
  * Route read-only search traffic to dedicated dedicated-pool nodes (reserved capacity) and fallback to hosted pool for bursts.

- Migration plan (high level):
  1) Export a representative shard (e.g., 100k vectors) and run a parallel reindex to compare recall.
  2) If acceptable, run incremental reindex with dual-write (VendorX + Redwood) for a week to validate metrics.
  3) Switch reads gradually (5/20/50/100) with canary monitoring.

I'll bring a short runbook and example SDK calls to the sync (node/python). Marissa — can you confirm the Thu 10/22 10am PT slot?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
